about: TL3's rubric (Q32), ported from TL1's src/trustladder/rubric.toml version 1. Every grade records this version. Raise it with any change that could change a grade; regrading under a new version adds grades and leaves the old ones as they are. Code grades whatever the facts settle; the judge grades the rest and cites its evidence. A later fact adds a grade and never changes one.

reliability.fact: fix rounds, later attempts and replans before the node merged; a node that closed without merging earns 1

grades.5: Merged first time: no fix round, later attempt or replan.
grades.4: Merged after one fix round, later attempt or replan.
grades.1: Merged after four or more, or closed without merging.

escalation.fact: questions to Rob plus incidents that needed him

grades.1: TL3 needed Rob four or more times.

queue.fact: times the merge queue sent the change back, or a merge with failing checks; ungraded when it didn't merge

grades.5: Merged on its first pass through the queue.
grades.4: Merged after the queue sent it back once.
grades.3: Merged after the queue sent it back twice.
grades.2: Merged after the queue sent it back three or more times.
grades.1: Merged with failing checks: CI failure escaped.

credit.fact: the credit ledger at close: start, earned, added, spent and balance; recorded, not graded

questions.fact: the kinds of the questions TL3 asked Rob; recorded, not graded

incidents.fact: the cause classes of the node's incidents, and how many needed Rob; recorded, not graded

phase_time.fact: seconds spent in each phase, from the phase history; recorded, not graded

tokens.fact: input, output and cache tokens summed over the node's MLflow traces, added by its postmortem; recorded, not graded

cache_rate.fact: the share of input tokens read from the prompt cache over the node's MLflow traces, added by its postmortem; recorded, not graded

grades.5: The brief asks for exactly what the request asks, reading any ambiguity the way Rob meant.
grades.4: The brief covers the request, with a minor gap or addition that changes nothing important.
grades.3: The brief covers the request's core but misses or adds a part a careful reader would notice.
grades.2: The brief misses a main part of the request, or adds work it didn't ask for.
grades.1: The brief solves a different problem from the request's.

grades.5: The change does what its goals say, with no defect a careful reviewer would find.
grades.4: The change is right, with a minor flaw that changes nothing important.
grades.3: The change mostly works but has a defect a careful reviewer would notice.
grades.2: The change has a defect that defeats a main goal.
grades.1: The change does not do what its goals say.

grades.5: The forecast came within a tenth of the actual peak context.
grades.1: Off by more than a factor of two, or the node ran out of room.

grades.5: The fix round fixed every reported problem and introduced none.
grades.3: The fix round fixed some reported problems.
grades.1: The fix round fixed nothing, or made it worse.

grades.5: The raised-effort attempt rescued the work.
grades.3: It made progress but needed a later step.

grades.5: The question or report led Rob to the right decision on its own.
grades.3: Rob needed more evidence than it gave.
grades.1: It misled Rob or hid the decision.
